title: Understanding One-hot Encoding
text: One-hot encoding is a method of representing categorical data as binary vectors. Each category is represented by a vector with a single high (1) bit and all other bits low (0).

title: Calculating Dimensions for One-hot Encoding
text: To calculate the dimensions for one-hot encoding, consider the number of unique categories you need to represent. For DNA strings, each letter (T, G, C, A) is a category.

title: Determine the Number of Unique Categories
text: How many unique categories (letters) are there in a DNA string?

title: Calculate the Total Number of Dimensions
text: If each DNA string has $$3000$$ letters and each letter can be one of $$4$$ categories, how many dimensions will the one-hot encoded vector have?

title: Understanding the Exponential Growth
text: The number of dimensions grows exponentially with the length of the DNA string when using one-hot encoding. This is because each position in the string can independently be one of $$4$$ categories.
